title: The List That Remembers
goal: Each call to add_item with no list should build a fresh list — but calls keep sharing one list.
code:
def add_item(item, items=[]):
    items.append(item)
    return items

print(add_item("a"))  # ['a'] — as expected
print(add_item("b"))  # ['a', 'b'] — surprise!
bug_criteria: Must identify the mutable default argument: the empty list in the signature is created ONCE at function definition, not per call, so every call appends to the same shared list. The fix is the None-sentinel pattern (default items=None, then items = items if items is not None else [] inside the body) — not deleting the default or copying at call time.
